card.name: Funaná
card.tagline: Cape Verde's accordion-and-iron dance of forbidden joy
card.profile: Funaná is a music and dance genre from Santiago island, Cape Verde, built on the diatonic accordion (gaita) with rhythm supplied by the ferrinho, a scraped iron rod (Wikipedia). It has a 2-beat rhythm at tempos from andante to vivace; as a couple dance, partners embrace with one arm and join hands with the other, marking the beat through quick, strong alternating knee flexions. It emerged among the Badiu of Santiago's rural interior, who turned a Portuguese-introduced accordion into a distinctly Cape Verdean sound.
card.insight: Suppressed as "primitive" under Portuguese colonial rule and danced informally at village festivities, funaná surged after independence in 1975 — modernized by Bulimundo and later Ferro Gaita — and was officially classified as National Intangible Cultural Heritage via Ordinance n.º 9/2024 (April 9, 2024) by Cape Verde's Ministry of Culture (Wikipedia; Cabo Verde).
